behavior: Interrupts a serious conversation to caution Maku about bottles, then praises his good heart.
Takes the oil bottle in both hands; for a moment neither she nor the child lets go.
After an astral return she says the child is cold and closes the latch instead of finishing her thought.
data.design: An elderly human keeper within a familiar Gen 3 household scale. World palette: muted coastal colors with small warm interior lights. Stage age through hands on a bottle, lamp work and careful domestic movements. These are scene directions, not approval of a new costume. Hair, clothing construction and final portrait design need an approved reference; Ellie is a working name. No occult insignia, monstrous anatomy or conspicuously sinister portrait.

description:
The lighthouse’s elderly sole keeper is teaching her child how to leave her. She knows she has little time left and wants the child prepared to live beyond her care. Her practical affection is in measured lamp oil, a trimmed wick and the larger slice of pie. She straightens a crease that is not there while telling the child they can go.

She speaks in plain domestic instructions, affectionate “love” and small corrections. When she evades a subject, she changes her action or leaves a sentence unfinished.

Mother performed the ritual on an already existing child and believes in the water entities’ mythology. The ritual served a religious purpose beyond the child’s welfare; its purpose and cost remain open. These are later revelations. The opening shows a keeper and parent, without cult emblems or explanations of arrested childhood. Later knowledge reinterprets her care as both love and containment; it does not make every affectionate scene insincere.
